title: Billing models
standfirst: The meter decides your bill more than the hourly rate does. Four shapes are in play: flat per size, per vCPU and per GB, a plan fee that returns as credit, and measured CPU.
idea: Flat per size: you pick a fixed shape and pay an hourly rate for it whether it works or waits. Boat, Sandboxer and Lizard work this way. It is the easiest to predict and the easiest to compare.

Per vCPU and per GB: the rate is a sum of parts, so much per vCPU-hour, per GB-hour of memory and per GB-month of disk. Agent 37, InstaBox, E2B and Vercel work this way, and boxd uses three meters of its own. It is flexible and hard to compare, because two providers can quote the same hourly number for different amounts of memory.

A plan fee that returns as credit: Sandboxer, InstaBox, Lizard and Boat sell a monthly plan whose dollars convert into usage. That is not a fee, but it is a floor: a light month still costs the plan price, and unused plan time usually expires. Morph's MCU model is a fourth shape: the rate is the largest resource dimension, not the sum.

splits.heading: Reserved size versus measured use
body: A flat rate bills the shape you reserved. A measured meter bills what the machine used, which can be much less or much more than the shape suggests. Runtime bills measured active CPU with a 50-millicore floor plus reserved memory. Sprites bills actual CPU and actual memory. Vercel bills active CPU excluding I/O wait, plus provisioned memory.

The difference is largest for an agent waiting on a model. Runtime's floor makes an idle-but-running box cost about $0.03 an hour; a flat 2 vCPU / 4 GiB shape costs its full hourly rate whether it waits or not.

splits.heading: The plan is a floor, not a fee
body: Boat's $20 plan buys $20 of VM time, and unused time expires monthly. Sandboxer's $20 buys about 555 default-hours, and the plan converts into machine time. InstaBox and Lizard treat the fee as a monthly credit that resets.
The trap is a workload that costs $3 of usage and still bills $20. That is not a pricing error; it is the floor doing its job.

splits.heading: What is still charged while stopped
body: Agent 37, InstaBox and Runtime charge storage. Sandboxer counts stopped storage against a free quota. Boat charges nothing and keeps the disk for 14 days. boxd charges for written disk in every state and for memory in standby. Lizard's stop deletes the sandbox. E2B does not bill paused or killed sandboxes, but volumes and snapshots are separate.
Vercel is the one to read carefully: persistent sandboxes save a snapshot on stop, and snapshot storage bills separately from compute.

watchFor: Whether the meter measures reserved size, actual CPU, or resident memory.
Whether the monthly fee returns as usage, and what expires at month end.
What is charged while stopped: compute, memory, storage, or nothing.
Which costs are absent from the pricing page: egress, snapshots, static IPs.
Whether there is a minimum billed duration or a one-minute increment.

rows.scenario: Priced from the reserved shape — $0.80 per vCPU-month and $0.70 per GB-month — so waiting costs the same as working.
rows.note: Prepaid wallet, per minute, priced from the reserved shape: $0.80 per vCPU-month, $0.70 per GB-month, $0.09 per GB-month of disk. No plan fee, no minimum, stopped time is disk only.

rows.scenario: Billed on allocated RAM per second with CPU included, so a waiting box pays for its whole memory allocation.
rows.note: Active compute is billed on allocated RAM per second at $0.0000115 per GB-second, with CPU included. Snapshots and volumes bill separately; tiers are wallet top-ups, not subscriptions.

rows.scenario: A flat hourly rate per size, $0.036 for the default 4 vCPU / 8 GB, whether it waits or works.
rows.note: A monthly plan that is prepaid machine time plus limits, with a separate dollar wallet for overage. Per second while running; stopped is zero machine time and the disk is kept 14 days.

source.quote: VM time past the included time | $0.036 per hour of `default`

rows.scenario: vCPU on the size while running, RAM on resident memory, disk on bytes written, so a waiting box pays for what it holds.
rows.note: Prepaid credits and three meters: vCPU on the size while running, RAM on resident memory (also in standby), disk on bytes written in every state. No plan fee; storage prices are unpublished.

source.quote: RAM bills on the memory a machine actually has resident, sampled every second, while it is running or in standby

rows.scenario: Per second of allocated vCPU and RAM while running, so the reserved shape sets the bill even when the agent waits.
rows.note: Per second of allocated vCPU and RAM while running, against a credit balance. Paused and killed sandboxes are not billed. Pro adds a $150 monthly fee; Hobby has a one-time $100 credit.

rows.scenario: A plan that is also credit, then per-second vCPU and RAM; a light month still costs the plan.
rows.note: A subscription that is also credit: $20, $100 or $500 a month, then per-second vCPU and RAM, GiB-hour storage and $0.02 per GiB of egress. Paused and stopped machines pay storage only.

rows.scenario: A flat hourly price per size, billed per second including idle, inside a $19 plan that includes $19 of usage.
rows.note: One $19 plan including $19 of usage; sandboxes are a flat hourly price per size, billed per second including idle, and volumes bill on used space. Snapshot storage has no published price.

source.quote: Pro costs $19 a month and includes $19 of usage for the whole platform: apps, databases, Sandboxes, storage and egress.

rows.scenario: MCUs where the rate is the largest resource dimension, so a memory-heavy idle box pays on memory.
rows.note: MCUs where the rate is the largest resource dimension: 1 vCPU-hour, 4 GB RAM-hours, 16 GB disk-hours or 5 TB snapshot-hours, at $0.05 per MCU-hour. Plans include MCU allocations.

rows.scenario: Measured active CPU above a 50-millicore floor plus reserved memory, so waiting costs about $0.03 an hour.
rows.note: Prepaid credit, per second: measured active CPU above a 50-millicore floor, plus reserved memory, plus storage while paused or stopped. No plan fee; plans are in a private beta.

source.quote: Measured CPU use above a 50-millicore floor

rows.scenario: A monthly plan whose dollars return as machine time at a fixed multiplier per size; stopped time is free.
rows.note: A monthly plan whose dollars return as machine time, metered per second at a fixed multiplier per size. Stopped time is free, but the $20 plan is a floor and plan time expires monthly.

rows.scenario: Actual CPU at $0.0385 per CPU-hour and actual memory at $0.021875 per GB-hour, so a waiting Sprite is cheap but not free.
rows.note: Actual CPU at $0.0385 per CPU-hour and actual memory at $0.021875 per GB-hour, plus hot and cold storage. The pricing page says there are no plans; the product FAQ describes plans.

rows.scenario: Active CPU excluding I/O wait plus provisioned memory, so memory is paid for while the CPU waits.
rows.note: Active CPU at $0.128 per CPU-hour excluding I/O wait, provisioned memory at $0.0212 per GB-hour with a one-minute minimum, plus creations, transfer, snapshots and drives.

scenario.title: One month of a box that mostly waits
scenario.setup: A 2 vCPU / 4 GB sandbox runs for 730 hours. The agent is busy for about 5% of that time and waits on a model for the rest. Nothing else changes.

beats.what: The machine is created and the agent starts. The meter is either the shape you reserved or the resources it uses.
The agent has been idle for most of it. On a reserved meter the bill is already fixed; on a measured meter it is nearly zero.
The invoice arrives, and the plan floor decides whether a cheap month is cheap.

scenario.turn: Two providers can quote the same hourly number for different amounts of memory. What separates them is whether the meter follows the reserved shape, the measured CPU, or the resident memory — and what the plan floor does to a light month.

questions: Does the meter measure the shape I reserved, or what the machine actually used?
Does the monthly fee return as usage, and what expires at the end of the month?
What is charged while stopped: compute, memory, storage, or nothing?
Which costs are missing from the pricing page — egress, snapshots, static IPs?
Is there a minimum billed duration or a one-minute increment, and how does it round?
